passage:
Sunday: Uma asked Mummy, "Can I teach the Class 5 kids in our lane after school? Their parents offered a small fee." Alka thought for a moment. "One hour, four days a week, and only after your own homework. I will talk to their parents first."

Two weeks later, Wednesday: Uma sat on the veranda with three children, a slate and a bag of chalk. She noted their trouble spots: fractions, spellings. By evening she was tired, but proud.

End of the month: Uma counted the fees on the table: six hundred rupees. She put half in Mummy's hand, "for the house," and half into a tin labelled Exam Fee. Alka pressed her hand and said nothing.

qa.q: How many days a week and how long each day did Alka allow Uma to teach?
qa.a: Alka allowed one hour, four days a week.

qa.q: How did Uma feel on the first Wednesday evening?
qa.a: Uma felt tired but proud after teaching three children.

qa.q: What else could Uma do to keep the earning study-safe, and why?
qa.a: Uma could set a fixed stopping time and skip the sessions in exam week, because study time protects the longer-term goal that the fee is meant for.

qa.q: How might Alka feel when Uma puts half the fees in her hand?
qa.a: Alka is probably moved and proud, which is why she presses Uma's hand and says nothing.

grounding: With parental permission the teen teaches Class 5 children after school for a small fee, keeps it modest and study-safe, and gives part to the household while saving part for exam fees.

passage: Pankaj, you want to earn a little? Your Rajni Mausi did too, at your age. The year my father fell ill, there wasn't much money. I was in Class 11. First I asked Amma and Bapuji if I could teach. They said yes, but only two children, only four days a week, and never past seven, because my own boards came first. So I taught two Class 5 girls from our lane, maths and English, at our kitchen table from five to six. Their mothers paid a small fee each month. I gave some of it to Amma for vegetables and kept some in a tin marked "exam fees". When the board registration came, the tin covered it. I was so proud. And my own marks didn't drop, because we had set those limits at the start.

qa.a: From five to six, at the kitchen table.

qa.q: How did young Rajni feel when the tin covered the exam fees?
qa.a: Young Rajni felt very proud, having earned it herself while keeping her own studies safe.

qa.q: Which choice at the start made the plan safe?
qa.a: Agreeing limits with Amma and Bapuji, two children, four days a week and never past seven, so earning never crowded out her boards.

qa.q: What might it have meant to Amma to receive part of the fee?
qa.a: Amma may have felt relieved and touched, since the help came from her daughter during a hard year.

grounding: An elder recalls tutoring Class 5 children with her parents' permission, keeping it modest and study-safe, and splitting the earnings between home and exam fees.

passage: The month Nandini's mother's stitching orders dried up, Nandini asked if she could tutor. Her parents agreed on conditions: weekends only, only until her own pre-boards, and they would meet the family first. Bidisha, a Class 5 girl from the next building, needed help with fractions. The complication was the power cuts; most Saturday evenings the lane went dark. So Nandini moved the lessons to Saturday and Sunday mornings, on the balcony, in daylight. Bidisha's mother paid a small fee at the end of each month. Nandini put part of it in her mother's kitchen tin without saying anything, and the rest in an envelope marked "Board exam form". When the pre-boards arrived, she paused the lessons for three weeks, as agreed. Bidisha sent her a drawing of a fraction pizza with "Good luck Didi" on it.

qa.q: Where did Nandini move the lessons?
qa.a: To Saturday and Sunday mornings, on the balcony, in daylight.

qa.q: How might Nandini feel receiving Bidisha's drawing?
qa.a: She probably felt touched and happy, seeing that the lessons mattered to Bidisha 😊.
The conditions agreed with her parents: weekends only, and a pause for her own pre-boards.

qa.q: What were the lessons like for Bidisha?
qa.a: Bidisha seems to have enjoyed them and grown fond of Nandini, sending a fraction pizza drawing to wish her luck.

grounding: Shows a teen tutoring a Class 5 child with parental permission, working around power cuts, keeping it study-safe and sharing earnings with the household.
